purpose: Deterministically identify the complete declared input evidence set used by a continuing-obligation reconstruction so independent reconstructions can establish whether they evaluated the same retained inputs without treating identity equality as proof of source authenticity, authority or completeness against external reality.

content_identity.rule: Digest the immutable source bytes or a declared canonical byte representation. A digest identifies committed content under the declared algorithm/canonicalization only; it does not prove authenticity, authority, legal validity, semantic correctness or completeness against evidence that was never supplied.

schema_rule_versions.rule: Comparison is version-bound. Every rule/schema version capable of changing validation disposition, lineage or projection must be declared.

canonicalization.record_order: Sort by record_kind, then record_ref, then immutable content digest. Ordering is identity-only and grants no temporal, predecessor, authenticity or authority precedence.
canonicalization.serialization: UTF-8 JSON with object keys sorted lexicographically, arrays retained in their schema-defined semantic order except record_inventory which uses record_order, no insignificant whitespace.

record_inventory.rule: Every record retained by the reconstruction manifest appears exactly once with its immutable content identity and reconstruction validation disposition. Equivalent duplicates remain distinct inventory entries.

inclusion_exclusion_inventory.rule: The three inventories must account for every record_inventory entry exactly once according to its reconstruction disposition; excluded records are part of evidence-set identity and cannot be omitted from the commitment.

aggregate_commitment.input_rule: Digest the canonical serialization of source coordinates, schema/rule versions, source identity inventory, complete record inventory and inclusion/exclusion inventory. Do not include evidence_set_commitment_id, committed_at or the aggregate digest itself.
aggregate_commitment.meaning: Equality proves only that the compared valid commitments declare identical canonical commitment inputs under the same comparison semantics.

comparison.SAME_EVIDENCE_SET: Both commitments are structurally valid and comparison-compatible, and source coordinates, schema/rule versions, canonicalization, source content identities, complete record identities and inclusion/exclusion inventories are identical; aggregate digests must also match.
comparison.DIFFERENT_EVIDENCE_SET: Both commitments are structurally valid and comparison-compatible, but one or more committed coordinates, versions, source identities, record identities or inclusion/exclusion inventory values differ. Report the differing committed fields; a matching projected state does not change this outcome.
comparison.FAIL_CLOSED_UNCOMPARABLE: Comparison compatibility or commitment integrity cannot be established, including missing/malformed required identity, unsupported or unresolved canonicalization/digest semantics, incomplete inventory accounting, or an aggregate digest inconsistent with the declared canonical inputs.
comparison.hash_boundary: Matching hashes never prove that source evidence is authentic, authoritative, legally effective, semantically valid, complete against external reality, or sufficient for a substantive projected state. Those remain governed by the projection/reconstruction validation rules.
comparison.collision_boundary: Digest equality is interpreted only under the declared algorithm and canonicalization assumptions; unresolved algorithm/canonicalization integrity fails closed.

authority_boundaries.rule: Evidence-set commitment and comparison establish declared input-set identity only. Creation, hashing, matching, signing, storage, publication or validation cannot create or expand commercial, contract/legal, payment, work, runtime, Task Registry or COSV authority.

prohibitions: No source authenticity inference from hash equality
No source authority inference from hash equality
